1	package jobsview
2	
3	import (
4		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
7		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
9	)
10	
11	// Init returns nothing.
12	//
13	// The view fetches nothing and starts no chain: its rows arrive in the
14	// broadcast, and switchView hands it the snapshot on the way in (sendJobsTo).
15	// A view that asked on arrival would be reading a second answer to a question
16	// the router already holds.
17	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
18	
19	// Update handles messages.
20	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
21		switch msg := msg.(type) {
22		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
23			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
24			return m, nil
25	
26		case jobs.ChangedMsg:
27			return m.handleJobsChanged(msg)
28	
29		case jobs.FrameMsg:
30			return m.handleFrameMsg(msg)
31	
32		case tea.KeyMsg:
33			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
34		}
35	
36		m.footer.Handle(msg)
37		return m, nil
38	}
39	
40	// handleJobsChanged takes the router's snapshot and rebuilds both tables.
41	//
42	// Both, not just the one on screen: the item table is what the cursor stands in
43	// while a target settles under it, and rebuilding it only on the way in would
44	// freeze it at the moment it was opened.
45	func (m Model) handleJobsChanged(msg jobs.ChangedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
46		m.runs = msg.Runs
47		m.refreshRows()
48		return m, nil
49	}
50	
51	// handleFrameMsg takes the animation's frame: the row spinners and the footer.
52	func (m Model) handleFrameMsg(msg jobs.FrameMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
53		m.frame = msg.Frame
54		m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)
55		m.refreshRows()
56		return m, nil
57	}
58	
59	// visibleRuns is what this view shows: the runs of the current context (D8).
60	// The table decides the order; this decides which exist.
61	func (m Model) visibleRuns() []jobs.Run {
62		return jobs.FilterContext(m.runs, m.contextName)
63	}
64	
65	// openedRun returns the run the item level is showing, and whether it is still
66	// in the snapshot.
67	//
68	// It can stop being: the registry keeps the last MaxFinishedRuns settled runs,
69	// so a run left open long enough is eventually pruned out from under the
70	// cursor. refreshRows is what answers for that.
71	func (m Model) openedRun() (jobs.Run, bool) {
72		for _, run := range m.visibleRuns() {
73			if run.ID == m.openRun {
74				return run, true
75			}
76		}
77		return jobs.Run{}, false
78	}
79	
80	// refreshRows rebuilds both tables from the snapshot, and falls back to the
81	// list when the run being shown has been pruned.
82	func (m *Model) refreshRows() {
83		runs := m.visibleRuns()
84		rows := make([]runRow, len(runs))
85		for i, run := range runs {
86			rows[i] = runRow{Run: run, Frame: m.frame}
87		}
88		m.runTable.SetItems(rows)
89	
90		run, ok := m.openedRun()
91		if m.level == levelItems && !ok {
92			// Back to the list rather than an empty table: the run is gone, so
93			// there is nothing to say about it, and a breadcrumb naming a label
94			// that no longer exists would be worse than no breadcrumb.
95			m.level = levelRuns
96			m.openRun = 0
97			m.itemTable.SetItems(nil)
98			return
99		}
100	
101		items := make([]itemRow, len(run.Items))
102		for i, item := range run.Items {
103			items[i] = itemRow{Item: item, Frame: m.frame}
104		}
105		m.itemTable.SetItems(items)
106	}
107	
108	// handleKeyMsg routes a key. The filter comes first (Rule 136): while it has
109	// the keyboard, every key is text.
110	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
111		if m.inFilter() {
112			return m.forwardToTable(msg)
113		}
114	
115		switch msg.String() {
116		case "right":
117			return m.openSelected()
118	
119		case "left", "esc":
120			return m.closeItems()
121	
122		case keymap.Kill:
123			return m.stopSelected()
124	
125		case ".":
126			return m.cycleSort()
127	
128		case "/":
129			return m.activateSearch()
130		}
131	
132		return m.forwardToTable(msg)
133	}
134	
135	// forwardToTable hands the key to whichever level is on screen.
136	//
137	// The two tables are datatable.Model over different types, so this is a branch
138	// rather than an interface: a common interface would have to be declared over
139	// FilterBar and Update in a package that owns neither, for two call sites.
140	func (m Model) forwardToTable(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
141		if m.level == levelItems {
142			return m, m.itemTable.Update(msg)
143		}
144		return m, m.runTable.Update(msg)
145	}
146	
147	// stopSelected asks the router to stop what the cursor is on: the run at the
148	// top level, one target inside a run.
149	//
150	// It asks rather than acts, like every other write to the registry: the router
151	// owns it, and a view holding a pointer to it is the thing D1 keeps out. What
152	// the view holds is the identifier, read off the row it is rendering.
153	func (m Model) stopSelected() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
154		if stop := m.availability().Stop; !stop.Enabled() {
155			return m, m.footer.Warn(stop.Reason)
156		}
157		if m.level == levelItems {
158			row, _ := m.itemTable.Selected()
159			return m, jobs.CancelItem(m.openRun, row.Item.Target)
160		}
161		row, _ := m.runTable.Selected()
162		return m, jobs.Cancel(row.Run.ID)
163	}
164	
165	// cycleSort moves the runs table on to its next sortable column.
166	//
167	// It is guarded rather than forwarded, so the refusal and the greying come from
168	// one calculation (Rule 130): the item table declares no comparator, and a `.`
169	// that silently did nothing there would be the `return m, nil` the rule exists
170	// to remove.
171	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
172		if sort := m.availability().Sort; !sort.Enabled() {
173			return m, m.footer.Warn(sort.Reason)
174		}
175		m.runTable.CycleSort()
176		return m, nil
177	}
178	
179	func (m Model) activateSearch() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
180		if m.level == levelItems {
181			return m, m.itemTable.FilterBar().ActivateSearch()
182		}
183		return m, m.runTable.FilterBar().ActivateSearch()
184	}
185	
186	// filterBar is the bar of the level on screen. The footer renders it and
187	// GetFooterHeight budgets for it (Rule 136).
188	func (m Model) filterBar() *sharedcomponents.FilterBar {
189		if m.level == levelItems {
190			return m.itemTable.FilterBar()
191		}
192		return m.runTable.FilterBar()
193	}
194	
195	func (m Model) inFilter() bool { return m.filterBar().InEditMode() }
196	
197	// InEditMode tells the router the filter has the keyboard (app.FormView).
198	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool { return m.inFilter() }
199	
200	// FilterBarVisible closes the viewport rectangle around the bar
201	// (app.FilterBarView).
202	func (m Model) FilterBarVisible() bool { return m.filterBar().IsVisible() }
203	
204	// openSelected drills into the run under the cursor (Rule 111: → descends).
205	func (m Model) openSelected() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
206		if open := m.availability().Open; !open.Enabled() {
207			return m, m.footer.Warn(open.Reason)
208		}
209		row, _ := m.runTable.Selected()
210		m.openRun = row.Run.ID
211		m.level = levelItems
212		m.itemTable.GotoTop()
213		m.refreshRows()
214		m.resize(m.width, m.height)
215		return m, nil
216	}
217	
218	// closeItems goes back up.
219	//
220	// At the top level there is nowhere to go, and that is not a refusal worth
221	// naming: `esc` is what a user presses to leave a screen, this view has none
222	// behind it, and a footer line on every stray esc would be noise. Rule 130
223	// greys the entry instead, which says the same thing before the key is pressed.
224	func (m Model) closeItems() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
225		if m.level == levelRuns {
226			return m, nil
227		}
228		m.level = levelRuns
229		m.openRun = 0
230		m.resize(m.width, m.height)
231		return m, nil
232	}
233	
234	// resize lays both tables out.
235	//
236	// Both, again: the item table is measured for the size it will be opened at, so
237	// → cannot show one frame of a table sized for a window that has since changed.
238	//
239	// The breadcrumb costs a line at the item level (Rule 123), and it is not
240	// subtracted here: it is rendered in the footer, so GetFooterHeight already
241	// asks the router for it, and taking it off the table too would take it twice.
242	func (m *Model) resize(width, height int) {
243		m.width = width
244		m.height = height
245	
246		m.runTable.Resize(width, max(height-1, 1))
247		m.itemTable.Resize(width, max(height-1, 1))
248	}

1	package jobsview
2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
7		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
8	)
9	
10	// The glyph vocabulary of both tables. One table, five states, and the two
11	// levels share it: a run that failed and the target that failed it read the
12	// same, which is what makes → feel like opening the row rather than arriving
13	// somewhere else.
14	//
15	// They are glyphs the application already has. A sixth codepoint for "queued"
16	// when IconPending is the clock the pipeline column already uses would be a
17	// second name for one idea (see the note on IconLock in theme/icons.go).
18	
19	// runStateGlyph is the run's state, or the shared spinner frame while it goes.
20	//
21	// Queued spins too. It is waiting on a worker rather than on nothing, the
22	// difference is in the State column, and a static clock next to a row whose
23	// counter is climbing reads as a stall.
24	func runStateGlyph(r runRow) string {
25		switch r.Run.State() {
26		case jobs.RunRunning, jobs.RunQueued:
27			return r.Frame
28		case jobs.RunFailed:
29			return theme.IconError
30		case jobs.RunCancelled:
31			return theme.IconCanceled
32		default:
33			return theme.IconOK
34		}
35	}
36	
37	// itemStateGlyph is the same for one target. An item that is queued does not
38	// spin: within a run, waiting for a worker is exactly what distinguishes it
39	// from the ones that are running, and that is the D6 distinction this level
40	// exists to show.
41	func itemStateGlyph(r itemRow) string {
42		switch r.Item.State {
43		case jobs.ItemRunning:
44			return r.Frame
45		case jobs.ItemQueued:
46			return theme.IconPending
47		case jobs.ItemFailed:
48			return theme.IconError
49		case jobs.ItemSkipped:
50			return theme.IconSkipped
51		default:
52			return theme.IconOK
53		}
54	}
55	
56	// runStateStyle colours a run.
57	//
58	// `done` gets the same green as every other success glyph in the application
59	// (Rule 121, theme.StatusOKStyle) — the status view colours "OK" the same
60	// way, and a jobs list is exactly the kind of screen where a reader scans for
61	// the one row that is not green. `failed` is what deserves to be found
62	// without reading. `cancelled` is a warning rather than an error: nothing
63	// broke, the user stopped it. `queued` is dim, the way a zero and a
64	// placeholder are: nothing has happened yet.
65	//
66	// `running` is left plain on purpose. The spinner in the glyph column already
67	// says it, it says it by moving, and a second answer in colour would be one
68	// more thing to keep in step.
69	func runStateStyle(state jobs.RunState) lipgloss.Style {
70		switch state {
71		case jobs.RunDone:
72			return theme.StatusOKStyle
73		case jobs.RunFailed:
74			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
75		case jobs.RunCancelled:
76			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
77		case jobs.RunQueued:
78			return theme.DimStyle
79		default:
80			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
81		}
82	}
83	
84	// itemStateStyle is the same table one level down. `skipped` joins the warning
85	// side: a sync refused on a dirty tree did not fail, and the reason is in the
86	// Detail column beside it.
87	func itemStateStyle(state jobs.ItemState) lipgloss.Style {
88		switch state {
89		case jobs.ItemDone:
90			return theme.StatusOKStyle
91		case jobs.ItemFailed:
92			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
93		case jobs.ItemSkipped:
94			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
95		case jobs.ItemQueued:
96			return theme.DimStyle
97		default:
98			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
99		}
100	}

1	// Package jobsview is the `:jobs` screen: what is running, and what has run
2	// this session.
3	//
4	// It owns no work and starts none. Every row comes from the snapshot the router
5	// broadcasts (jobs.ChangedMsg), which is what lets this view exist at all — a
6	// screen that had to ask each view what it was doing would be the fifth
7	// bookkeeping internal/jobs removed.
8	package jobsview
9	
10	import (
11		"strconv"
12		"strings"
13	
14		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
15	
16		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/config"
17		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
18		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
19		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
20		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
21	)
22	
23	// level is which of the two tables is on screen (D2).
24	//
25	// A level rather than a tab: the second table is *about* a row of the first, so
26	// it is reached with → and left with ← or esc, the way every drill-down in the
27	// application is (Rule 111). Tabs would say the two are siblings.
28	type level int
29	
30	const (
31		levelRuns level = iota
32		levelItems
33	)
34	
35	// runRow and itemRow carry the spinner frame onto the row.
36	//
37	// The frame changes ten times a second and the columns are built once, in New,
38	// closing over nothing — so a Cell cannot reach the model to ask for it. Putting
39	// it on the row is what oci_resources does with imageRow, and for the same
40	// reason.
41	//
42	// It is the router's frame (D5): the one chain, taken bare from the router's
43	// frame message (not from jobs.ChangedMsg) because a table cell is measured before it is styled (Rule 122). Using
44	// datatable's own AdvanceSpinner here would be a second chain beside it.
45	type runRow struct {
46		Run   jobs.Run
47		Frame string
48	}
49	
50	type itemRow struct {
51		Item  jobs.Item
52		Frame string
53	}
54	
55	// Model is the jobs view.
56	type Model struct {
57		// runs is the snapshot, every context included. contextName is what the
58		// tables filter it by: a run is kept for the session and stamped, so a
59		// context switch hides its runs rather than dropping them (D8).
60		runs        []jobs.Run
61		contextName string
62	
63		// frame is the router's bare spinner frame.
64		frame string
65	
66		level   level
67		openRun jobs.JobID
68	
69		runTable  datatable.Model[runRow]
70		itemTable datatable.Model[itemRow]
71	
72		footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
73	
74		width, height int
75	}
76	
77	// Column indexes of the runs table.
78	//
79	// Only runColumnStarted is referred to — it is what the table opens sorted by —
80	// and the rest of the block is what makes it right: written as `= 5` it would
81	// go on compiling, and start naming another column, the day one is inserted
82	// above it. That is the failure the containers table records in the note above
83	// columnPorts.
84	const (
85		runColumnState = iota
86		runColumnKind
87		runColumnLabel
88		runColumnProgress
89		runColumnStateText
90		runColumnStarted
91	)
92	
93	// New builds the view. The context comes from the router.
94	//
95	// It is passed rather than read back from the configuration, for D68's reason
96	// one screen over: the router is what knows which context is current, and a
97	// view reading it again would be a second answer to a settled question. The
98	// router also drops every view on a switch (reinitializeViews), so the name
99	// cannot go stale.
100	func New(_ *config.Config, contextName string) Model {
101		return Model{
102			contextName: contextName,
103			runTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[runRow]{
104				Columns: runColumns(),
105				// Newest first. A jobs list is read to find out what is happening
106				// now, and ascending would pin the session's first run to the top
107				// for the rest of the session.
108				SortColumn: runColumnStarted,
109				SortDesc:   true,
110			}),
111			itemTable: datatable.New(datatable.Config[itemRow]{
112				Columns: itemColumns(),
113				// The order the batch was dispatched in. It is the only order that
114				// means anything here — the targets of a run have no natural rank,
115				// and sorting by state would move a row out from under the cursor
116				// every time one settled.
117				SortColumn: -1,
118			}),
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// runColumns describes the runs table.
123	//
124	// The first column is the run's **state**, not its kind, and it is also where
125	// the spinner goes. That is the containers table's shape and it is deliberate:
126	// a jobs list is scanned to find the one that failed and the one still going,
127	// so the glyph answers the question the reader arrived with, and the Kind
128	// column says in a word what sort of work it was.
129	//
130	// A state glyph column colours by the semantic status styles rather than by a
131	// theme.IconStyle role, which is the choice the containers table already makes.
132	// Roles exist for icons that name an *object* — a namespace, a repository, an
133	// image — where a palette should be able to tell them apart. A state has a
134	// colour already, and five new roles would give a theme five ways to make
135	// "failed" not red.
136	//
137	// The glyph and the State word are not the redundancy that a glyph beside its
138	// own name usually is: the glyph column doubles as the spinner while the run
139	// goes, and the word is what separates the four settled outcomes — "cancelled"
140	// from "failed" above all, which is the distinction Run.cancelled exists for.
141	func runColumns() []datatable.Column[runRow] {
142		return []datatable.Column[runRow]{
143			{
144				Title: "", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: datatable.IconColumnWidth,
145				Cell:  func(r runRow) string { return runStateGlyph(r) },
146				Style: func(r runRow) lipgloss.Style { return runStateStyle(r.Run.State()) },
147			},
148			{
149				Title: "Kind", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 8,
150				Cell: func(r runRow) string { return string(r.Run.Kind) },
151				Less: func(a, b runRow) bool { return a.Run.Kind < b.Run.Kind },
152				// The state is searchable here rather than through its own column,
153				// so `/failed` and `/scan` both work while the glyph column stays
154				// out of the filter (Rule 125).
155				Search: func(r runRow) string { return string(r.Run.Kind) + " " + string(r.Run.State()) },
156			},
157			{
158				Title: "Label", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent,
159				MinWidth: 14, MaxWidth: 40, Flex: 2, TruncateHead: true,
160				Cell:   func(r runRow) string { return r.Run.Label },
161				Less:   func(a, b runRow) bool { return strings.ToLower(a.Run.Label) < strings.ToLower(b.Run.Label) },
162				Search: func(r runRow) string { return r.Run.Label },
163			},
164			{
165				Title: "Progress", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 9,
166				Cell: func(r runRow) string { return progressCell(r.Run) },
167				// By how far along, not by how many: 1/2 is further than 3/12, and
168				// comparing the numerators would rank the bigger batch higher for
169				// having more left to do.
170				Less: func(a, b runRow) bool { return fraction(a.Run) < fraction(b.Run) },
171			},
172			{
173				Title: "State", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
174				Cell:  func(r runRow) string { return string(r.Run.State()) },
175				Style: func(r runRow) lipgloss.Style { return runStateStyle(r.Run.State()) },
176				Less:  func(a, b runRow) bool { return a.Run.State() < b.Run.State() },
177			},
178			{
179				Title: "Started", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 12,
180				Cell: func(r runRow) string { return theme.TimeAgo(r.Run.StartedAt) },
181				Less: func(a, b runRow) bool { return a.Run.StartedAt.Before(b.Run.StartedAt) },
182			},
183		}
184	}
185	
186	// itemColumns describes one run's targets.
187	//
188	// No Started column: an item has no timestamp of its own, and every target of a
189	// batch shares the run's. What an item has that a run does not is Detail — the
190	// reason a sync was skipped, the fact a scan failed — and that is what the
191	// width is worth spending on here.
192	func itemColumns() []datatable.Column[itemRow] {
193		return []datatable.Column[itemRow]{
194			{
195				Title: "", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: datatable.IconColumnWidth,
196				Cell:  func(r itemRow) string { return itemStateGlyph(r) },
197				Style: func(r itemRow) lipgloss.Style { return itemStateStyle(r.Item.State) },
198			},
199			{
200				Title: "Target", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent,
201				MinWidth: 20, MaxWidth: 60, Flex: 3, TruncateHead: true,
202				Cell:   func(r itemRow) string { return r.Item.Name() },
203				Search: func(r itemRow) string { return r.Item.Name() },
204			},
205			{
206				Title: "State", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
207				Cell:   func(r itemRow) string { return string(r.Item.State) },
208				Style:  func(r itemRow) lipgloss.Style { return itemStateStyle(r.Item.State) },
209				Search: func(r itemRow) string { return string(r.Item.State) },
210			},
211			{
212				Title: "Detail", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 10, Flex: 2,
213				Cell:   func(r itemRow) string { return dashIfEmpty(r.Item.Detail) },
214				Style:  func(r itemRow) lipgloss.Style { return detailStyle(r.Item) },
215				Search: func(r itemRow) string { return r.Item.Detail },
216			},
217		}
218	}
219	
220	// progressCell is the "7/12" of a run.
221	//
222	// A settled run keeps it. "12/12" beside "3/12" is what makes the size of a
223	// batch readable at a glance, and blanking it once the run is over would empty
224	// the column for most of the list.
225	func progressCell(r jobs.Run) string {
226		return strconv.Itoa(r.Done()) + "/" + strconv.Itoa(r.Total())
227	}
228	
229	// fraction is how far along a run is, in [0,1]. An empty run is finished.
230	func fraction(r jobs.Run) float64 {
231		if r.Total() == 0 {
232			return 1
233		}
234		return float64(r.Done()) / float64(r.Total())
235	}
236	
237	// dashIfEmpty is the placeholder for a cell with nothing in it — a dash rather
238	// than a blank, so the column still reads as a column (Rule 122).
239	func dashIfEmpty(s string) string {
240		if s == "" {
241			return "-"
242		}
243		return s
244	}
245	
246	// detailStyle dims the placeholder and leaves a real detail alone.
247	//
248	// "already there" or "scan failed — check logs" is what the column exists for,
249	// so dimming it would grey out exactly what the reader came to read. What is
250	// dim is the absence, which is Rule 122's rule for a zero.
251	func detailStyle(i jobs.Item) lipgloss.Style {
252		if i.Detail == "" {
253			return theme.DimStyle
254		}
255		return lipgloss.NewStyle()
256	}

1	package jobsview
2	
3	import (
4		"strconv"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
8		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/help"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
13	)
14	
15	// GetTitle names the view, and the run when one is open.
16	func (m Model) GetTitle() string {
17		base := theme.IconHourglass + " Jobs"
18		if run, ok := m.openedRun(); ok && m.level == levelItems {
19			return base + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " " + run.Label
20		}
21		return base
22	}
23	
24	// GetIcon returns the view icon. The title carries it, as everywhere else.
25	func (m Model) GetIcon() string { return "" }
26	
27	// GetHeaderInfo says how much of the session is on screen.
28	//
29	// Running first, because it is why the view is open. The total is the runs of
30	// this context, which is what the table holds — not the registry's, which also
31	// counts the ones a context switch is hiding.
32	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(_ string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
33		runs := m.visibleRuns()
34		return []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
35			{Key: "Running", Value: strconv.Itoa(len(jobs.Unfinished(runs))), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
36			{Key: "Runs", Value: strconv.Itoa(len(runs)), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
37		}
38	}
39	
40	// GetShortcuts returns the header's shortcut column (Rules 130, 137, 138).
41	//
42	// The obvious keys are absent: ↑↓, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End. What is left is
43	// the drill, the sort, the filter and help — and the three that vary are greyed
44	// rather than dropped, so the column is the same four lines at both levels.
45	func (m Model) GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
46		a := m.availability()
47		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
48			{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Stop", Disabled: !a.Stop.Enabled()},
49			{Key: "→", Description: "Open targets", Disabled: !a.Open.Enabled()},
50			{Key: "esc", Description: "Go back", Disabled: !a.Close.Enabled()},
51			{Key: ".", Description: "Sort", Disabled: !a.Sort.Enabled()},
52			{Key: "/", Description: "Filter"},
53			{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
54		}
55	}
56	
57	// GetFooterHeight budgets the footer (Rules 124, 136).
58	//
59	// The breadcrumb is a line of the footer at the item level, and the filter bar
60	// adds its own when visible. Both are asked for here so the router can take
61	// them off the viewport.
62	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
63		height := 2 + m.filterBar().ExtraHeight()
64		if m.level == levelItems {
65			height++
66		}
67		return height
68	}
69	
70	// RenderFooter renders the lines below the viewport (Rule 124).
71	//
72	// Order: breadcrumb, filter bar, blank, message. The breadcrumb sits directly
73	// under the table because it names the level the table is showing (Rule 123).
74	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
75		var parts []string
76		if m.level == levelItems {
77			parts = append(parts, m.renderBreadcrumb(width))
78		}
79		if bar := m.filterBar(); bar.IsVisible() {
80			parts = append(parts, bar.View())
81		}
82		parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), m.footer.View(width, m.status()))
83		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
84	}
85	
86	// renderBreadcrumb is the trail below the table at the item level (Rule 123).
87	// Breadcrumb mode: it is not navigable, the level shown is highlighted and the
88	// one above it is dimmed.
89	func (m Model) renderBreadcrumb(width int) string {
90		run, ok := m.openedRun()
91		if !ok {
92			return theme.EmptyLineBg(width)
93		}
94		tabs := []theme.TabItem{
95			{Label: "Runs"},
96			{Label: string(run.Kind) + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " " + run.Label},
97		}
98		return theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+theme.RenderTabs(tabs, 1), width)
99	}
100	
101	// status is the derived line, with no timer (Rule 128).
102	//
103	// It is the shared sentence every other footer says while work runs, and it is
104	// asked for with no origin: this view launched none of it, so the detailed form
105	// would be a lie about ownership. What it says instead is the count — which is
106	// also the one form that does not end in ":jobs for details", because that is
107	// where the reader already is.
108	func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
109		live := jobs.Unfinished(m.visibleRuns())
110		if len(live) == 0 {
111			return sharedcomponents.Status{}
112		}
113		return sharedcomponents.Status{
114			Text:    sharedcomponents.Plural(len(live), "job", "jobs") + " running",
115			Spinner: true,
116		}
117	}
118	
119	// View renders the table of the level on screen.
120	//
121	// There is no loading branch: this view fetches nothing, so it is never between
122	// a request and an answer. A table with nothing to show still renders its
123	// header and no rows (datatable.View() does this on its own) — the count that
124	// says why (zero runs, or a filter matching none of them) lives in the header
125	// (GetHeaderInfo), not in the body.
126	func (m Model) View() string {
127		if m.level == levelItems {
128			return m.itemTable.View()
129		}
130		return m.runTable.View()
131	}
132	
133	// GetHelpContent returns the help for `?` (Rule 114).
134	func (m Model) GetHelpContent() help.Content {
135		return help.Content{
136			Title: "Jobs",
137			Description: "Everything long-running the application has started this session: scans, syncs, clones, image pulls and deletes. " +
138				"A run is one batch started in one go from one view; press → to see the targets it holds. " +
139				"This view starts nothing and owns nothing — it reads the same record every other view reads.",
140			KeyBindings: []help.KeyBinding{
141				{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Stop the selected run, or the selected target inside one"},
142				{Key: "→", Description: "Open the selected run and list its targets"},
143				{Key: "esc", Description: "Go back to the list of runs"},
144				{Key: ".", Description: "Cycle the sort column (runs only). Each press toggles asc/desc, then moves to the next column"},
145				{Key: "/", Description: "Filter by kind, state, label or target"},
146				{Key: "↑/↓", Description: "Move the selection"},
147				{Key: "ctrl+p", Description: "Open command mode"},
148				{Key: "?", Description: "Show this help"},
149			},
150			Sections: []help.Section{
151				{
152					Title: "Runs",
153					Body: "State (first, untitled): a spinner while the run is queued or going, " +
154						theme.IconOK + " done, " + theme.IconError + " failed, " + theme.IconCanceled + " cancelled.\n" +
155						"Kind: what the run does — scan, sync, clone, pull, create, delete, index (the forge listing the explorer and its g read, refreshed when a session opens).\n" +
156						"Label: what the batch was launched on — the directory, the registry, the repository.\n" +
157						"Progress: targets settled over targets held. A target that was skipped or that failed has settled: progress reports on what is left to wait for, not on what succeeded.\n" +
158						"State: queued, running, done, failed or cancelled. A run is failed as soon as one of its targets is, and cancelled beats failed — a run stopped on purpose reads cancelled even though its targets failed because of it.\n" +
159						"Started: when the run was admitted, relative.",
160				},
161				{
162					Title: "Targets",
163					Body: "State (first, untitled): " + theme.IconPending + " queued, a spinner while running, " +
164						theme.IconOK + " done, " + theme.IconSkipped + " skipped, " + theme.IconError + " failed.\n" +
165						"Target: the repository path, the image reference, the group.\n" +
166						"State: queued and running are different things — queued is waiting for a worker, running is holding one. A batch of twelve on four workers is four running and eight queued.\n" +
167						"Detail: what the state alone cannot say — why a sync was skipped, that a scan failed. A dash means there was nothing to add.\n\n" +
168						"The order is the one the batch was dispatched in, and it does not change: sorting by state would move a row out from under the cursor every time one settled.",
169				},
170				{
171					Title: "What is listed",
172					Body: "Runs of the current context only. A run is stamped with the context it started in and kept for the session, so switching context hides them rather than dropping them — switching back brings them back.\n\n" +
173						"The last 20 settled runs are kept. A run still going is never dropped, however many have settled.",
174				},
175				{
176					Title: "Stopping work",
177					Body: "'" + keymap.Kill + "' on a run stops its queue: nothing further starts, whatever the kind. Targets still waiting are marked skipped, and the ones already running report their own outcome when they get there — a run that was stopped reads 'cancelled' rather than 'done', which is the distinction the list exists to keep.\n\n" +
178						"'" + keymap.Kill + "' on a single target is offered only where cutting the work leaves nothing behind: a scan and an image pull can be cut, a clone cannot — a half-written repository on disk is worse than one that finished. A sync waits out the fetch in flight, and a delete is never cut at all.\n\n" +
179						"The key is greyed when there is nothing to stop, and pressing it then says why in the footer rather than doing nothing.",
180				},
181				{
182					Title: "Where the rows come from",
183					Body: "The router owns one record of what is running and hands every view a copy of it. That is why a scan started in the workspaces list shows up here, and why the security inventory marks a row that this view also lists — it is the same work, recorded once.\n\n" +
184						"Nothing on this screen is fetched, so there is nothing to refresh: the rows change when the work does.",
185				},
186			},
187		}

1	package jobsview
2	
3	import (
4		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
7		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
9	)
10	
11	// Init returns nothing.
12	//
13	// The view fetches nothing and starts no chain: its rows arrive in the
14	// broadcast, and switchView hands it the snapshot on the way in (sendJobsTo).
15	// A view that asked on arrival would be reading a second answer to a question
16	// the router already holds.
17	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
18	
19	// Update handles messages.
20	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
21		switch msg := msg.(type) {
22		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
23			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
24			return m, nil
25	
26		case jobs.ChangedMsg:
27			return m.handleJobsChanged(msg)
28	
29		case jobs.FrameMsg:
30			return m.handleFrameMsg(msg)
31	
32		case tea.KeyMsg:
33			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
34		}
35	
36		m.footer.Handle(msg)
37		return m, nil
38	}
39	
40	// handleJobsChanged takes the router's snapshot and rebuilds both tables.
41	//
42	// Both, not just the one on screen: the item table is what the cursor stands in
43	// while a target settles under it, and rebuilding it only on the way in would
44	// freeze it at the moment it was opened.
45	func (m Model) handleJobsChanged(msg jobs.ChangedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
46		m.runs = msg.Runs
47		m.refreshRows()
48		return m, nil
49	}
50	
51	// handleFrameMsg takes the animation's frame: the row spinners and the footer.
52	func (m Model) handleFrameMsg(msg jobs.FrameMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
53		m.frame = msg.Frame
54		m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)
55		m.refreshRows()
56		return m, nil
57	}
58	
59	// visibleRuns is what this view shows: the runs of the current context (D8).
60	// The table decides the order; this decides which exist.
61	func (m Model) visibleRuns() []jobs.Run {
62		return jobs.FilterContext(m.runs, m.contextName)
63	}
64	
65	// openedRun returns the run the item level is showing, and whether it is still
66	// in the snapshot.
67	//
68	// It can stop being: the registry keeps the last MaxFinishedRuns settled runs,
69	// so a run left open long enough is eventually pruned out from under the
70	// cursor. refreshRows is what answers for that.
71	func (m Model) openedRun() (jobs.Run, bool) {
72		for _, run := range m.visibleRuns() {
73			if run.ID == m.openRun {
74				return run, true
75			}
76		}
77		return jobs.Run{}, false
78	}
79	
80	// refreshRows rebuilds both tables from the snapshot, and falls back to the
81	// list when the run being shown has been pruned.
82	func (m *Model) refreshRows() {
83		runs := m.visibleRuns()
84		rows := make([]runRow, len(runs))
85		for i, run := range runs {
86			rows[i] = runRow{Run: run, Frame: m.frame}
87		}
88		m.runTable.SetItems(rows)
89	
90		run, ok := m.openedRun()
91		if m.level == levelItems && !ok {
92			// Back to the list rather than an empty table: the run is gone, so
93			// there is nothing to say about it, and a breadcrumb naming a label
94			// that no longer exists would be worse than no breadcrumb.
95			m.level = levelRuns
96			m.openRun = 0
97			m.itemTable.SetItems(nil)
98			return
99		}
100	
101		items := make([]itemRow, len(run.Items))
102		for i, item := range run.Items {
103			items[i] = itemRow{Item: item, Frame: m.frame}
104		}
105		m.itemTable.SetItems(items)
106	}
107	
108	// handleKeyMsg routes a key. The filter comes first (Rule 136): while it has
109	// the keyboard, every key is text.
110	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
111		if m.inFilter() {
112			return m.forwardToTable(msg)
113		}
114	
115		switch msg.String() {
116		case "right":
117			return m.openSelected()
118	
119		case "left", "esc":
120			return m.closeItems()
121	
122		case keymap.Kill:
123			return m.stopSelected()
124	
125		case ".":
126			return m.cycleSort()
127	
128		case "/":
129			return m.activateSearch()
130		}
131	
132		return m.forwardToTable(msg)
133	}
134	
135	// forwardToTable hands the key to whichever level is on screen.
136	//
137	// The two tables are datatable.Model over different types, so this is a branch
138	// rather than an interface: a common interface would have to be declared over
139	// FilterBar and Update in a package that owns neither, for two call sites.
140	func (m Model) forwardToTable(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
141		if m.level == levelItems {
142			return m, m.itemTable.Update(msg)
143		}
144		return m, m.runTable.Update(msg)
145	}
146	
147	// stopSelected asks the router to stop what the cursor is on: the run at the
148	// top level, one target inside a run.
149	//
150	// It asks rather than acts, like every other write to the registry: the router
151	// owns it, and a view holding a pointer to it is the thing D1 keeps out. What
152	// the view holds is the identifier, read off the row it is rendering.
153	func (m Model) stopSelected() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
154		if stop := m.availability().Stop; !stop.Enabled() {
155			return m, m.footer.Warn(stop.Reason)
156		}
157		if m.level == levelItems {
158			row, _ := m.itemTable.Selected()
159			return m, jobs.CancelItem(m.openRun, row.Item.Target)
160		}
161		row, _ := m.runTable.Selected()
162		return m, jobs.Cancel(row.Run.ID)
163	}
164	
165	// cycleSort moves the runs table on to its next sortable column.
166	//
167	// It is guarded rather than forwarded, so the refusal and the greying come from
168	// one calculation (Rule 130): the item table declares no comparator, and a `.`
169	// that silently did nothing there would be the `return m, nil` the rule exists
170	// to remove.
171	func (m Model) cycleSort() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
172		if sort := m.availability().Sort; !sort.Enabled() {
173			return m, m.footer.Warn(sort.Reason)
174		}
175		m.runTable.CycleSort()
176		return m, nil
177	}
178	
179	func (m Model) activateSearch() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
180		if m.level == levelItems {
181			return m, m.itemTable.FilterBar().ActivateSearch()
182		}
183		return m, m.runTable.FilterBar().ActivateSearch()
184	}
185	
186	// filterBar is the bar of the level on screen. The footer renders it and
187	// GetFooterHeight budgets for it (Rule 136).
188	func (m Model) filterBar() *sharedcomponents.FilterBar {
189		if m.level == levelItems {
190			return m.itemTable.FilterBar()
191		}
192		return m.runTable.FilterBar()
193	}
194	
195	func (m Model) inFilter() bool { return m.filterBar().InEditMode() }
196	
197	// InEditMode tells the router the filter has the keyboard (app.FormView).
198	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool { return m.inFilter() }
199	
200	// FilterBarVisible closes the viewport rectangle around the bar
201	// (app.FilterBarView).
202	func (m Model) FilterBarVisible() bool { return m.filterBar().IsVisible() }
203	
204	// openSelected drills into the run under the cursor (Rule 111: → descends).
205	func (m Model) openSelected() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
206		if open := m.availability().Open; !open.Enabled() {
207			return m, m.footer.Warn(open.Reason)
208		}
209		row, _ := m.runTable.Selected()
210		m.openRun = row.Run.ID
211		m.level = levelItems
212		m.itemTable.GotoTop()
213		m.refreshRows()
214		m.resize(m.width, m.height)
215		return m, nil
216	}
217	
218	// closeItems goes back up.
219	//
220	// At the top level there is nowhere to go, and that is not a refusal worth
221	// naming: `esc` is what a user presses to leave a screen, this view has none
222	// behind it, and a footer line on every stray esc would be noise. Rule 130
223	// greys the entry instead, which says the same thing before the key is pressed.
224	func (m Model) closeItems() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
225		if m.level == levelRuns {
226			return m, nil
227		}
228		m.level = levelRuns
229		m.openRun = 0
230		m.resize(m.width, m.height)
231		return m, nil
232	}
233	
234	// resize lays both tables out.
235	//
236	// Both, again: the item table is measured for the size it will be opened at, so
237	// → cannot show one frame of a table sized for a window that has since changed.
238	//
239	// The breadcrumb costs a line at the item level (Rule 123), and it is not
240	// subtracted here: it is rendered in the footer, so GetFooterHeight already
241	// asks the router for it, and taking it off the table too would take it twice.
242	func (m *Model) resize(width, height int) {
243		m.width = width
244		m.height = height
245	
246		m.runTable.Resize(width, max(height-1, 1))
247		m.itemTable.Resize(width, max(height-1, 1))
248	}

2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
7		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
8	)
9	
10	// The glyph vocabulary of both tables. One table, five states, and the two
11	// levels share it: a run that failed and the target that failed it read the
12	// same, which is what makes → feel like opening the row rather than arriving
13	// somewhere else.
14	//
15	// They are glyphs the application already has. A sixth codepoint for "queued"
16	// when IconPending is the clock the pipeline column already uses would be a
17	// second name for one idea (see the note on IconLock in theme/icons.go).
18	
19	// runStateGlyph is the run's state, or the shared spinner frame while it goes.
20	//
21	// Queued spins too. It is waiting on a worker rather than on nothing, the
22	// difference is in the State column, and a static clock next to a row whose
23	// counter is climbing reads as a stall.
24	func runStateGlyph(r runRow) string {
25		switch r.Run.State() {
26		case jobs.RunRunning, jobs.RunQueued:
27			return r.Frame
28		case jobs.RunFailed:
29			return theme.IconError
30		case jobs.RunCancelled:
31			return theme.IconCanceled
32		default:
33			return theme.IconOK
34		}
35	}
36	
37	// itemStateGlyph is the same for one target. An item that is queued does not
38	// spin: within a run, waiting for a worker is exactly what distinguishes it
39	// from the ones that are running, and that is the D6 distinction this level
40	// exists to show.
41	func itemStateGlyph(r itemRow) string {
42		switch r.Item.State {
43		case jobs.ItemRunning:
44			return r.Frame
45		case jobs.ItemQueued:
46			return theme.IconPending
47		case jobs.ItemFailed:
48			return theme.IconError
49		case jobs.ItemSkipped:
50			return theme.IconSkipped
51		default:
52			return theme.IconOK
53		}
54	}
55	
56	// runStateStyle colours a run.
57	//
58	// `done` gets the same green as every other success glyph in the application
59	// (Rule 121, theme.StatusOKStyle) — the status view colours "OK" the same
60	// way, and a jobs list is exactly the kind of screen where a reader scans for
61	// the one row that is not green. `failed` is what deserves to be found
62	// without reading. `cancelled` is a warning rather than an error: nothing
63	// broke, the user stopped it. `queued` is dim, the way a zero and a
64	// placeholder are: nothing has happened yet.
65	//
66	// `running` is left plain on purpose. The spinner in the glyph column already
67	// says it, it says it by moving, and a second answer in colour would be one
68	// more thing to keep in step.
69	func runStateStyle(state jobs.RunState) lipgloss.Style {
70		switch state {
71		case jobs.RunDone:
72			return theme.StatusOKStyle
73		case jobs.RunFailed:
74			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
75		case jobs.RunCancelled:
76			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
77		case jobs.RunQueued:
78			return theme.DimStyle
79		default:
80			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
81		}
82	}
83	
84	// itemStateStyle is the same table one level down. `skipped` joins the warning
85	// side: a sync refused on a dirty tree did not fail, and the reason is in the
86	// Detail column beside it.
87	func itemStateStyle(state jobs.ItemState) lipgloss.Style {
88		switch state {
89		case jobs.ItemDone:
90			return theme.StatusOKStyle
91		case jobs.ItemFailed:
92			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
93		case jobs.ItemSkipped:
94			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
95		case jobs.ItemQueued:
96			return theme.DimStyle
97		default:
98			return lipgloss.NewStyle()
99		}
100	}

1	// Package indicator defines the activity states a table row's first column can
2	// show, their glyphs, and the precedence between concurrent sources of state.
3	// It is pure: no dependency on theme, jobs or datatable.
4	package indicator
5	
6	// State is what the first column says about a row. The zero value is Idle (rest).
7	type State int
8	
9	const (
10		Idle       State = iota // the row's own icon, or an empty cell
11		Running                 // blinks; busy counts as Running
12		Queued                  // waiting
13		Failed                  // op failed, container dead or exited non-zero
14		Suspended               // agent idle, container paused
15		Restarting              // container restarting
16		Done                    // job done, agent done
17		Cancelled               // job cancelled
18		Skipped                 // job skipped, container exited 0
19		Unknown                 // agent unknown, container created
20	)
21	
22	// states lists every state but Idle, in declaration order.
23	var states = []State{Running, Queued, Failed, Suspended, Restarting, Done, Cancelled, Skipped, Unknown}
24	
25	var names = map[State]string{
26		Idle: "idle", Running: "running", Queued: "queued", Failed: "failed",
27		Suspended: "suspended", Restarting: "restarting", Done: "done",
28		Cancelled: "cancelled", Skipped: "skipped", Unknown: "unknown",
29	}
30	
31	var glyphs = map[State]string{
32		Queued: "◴", Failed: "⊗", Suspended: "◐", Restarting: "◕",
33		Done: "◉", Cancelled: "⊘", Skipped: "⊖", Unknown: "◌",
34	}
35	
36	const (
37		runningOn  = "●"
38		runningOff = "○"
39	)
40	
41	// States returns every state but Idle, in declaration order.
42	func States() []State { return append([]State(nil), states...) }
43	
44	// Glyph returns the one-rune glyph of s; on is the blink phase (Running only).
45	// Idle has no glyph and yields an empty string.
46	func Glyph(s State, on bool) string {
47		if s == Running {
48			if on {
49				return runningOn
50			}
51			return runningOff
52		}
53		return glyphs[s]
54	}
55	
56	// Animated reports whether s blinks.
57	func Animated(s State) bool { return s == Running }
58	
59	// String returns the lowercase name of s.
60	func (s State) String() string {
61		if n, ok := names[s]; ok {
62			return n
63		}
64		return "invalid"
65	}
66	
67	// Activity is everything that can be true of one row at once.
68	type Activity struct {
69		Running, Queued, Failed bool  // Failed = a remembered failure
70		Observed                State // computed by the view; Idle if none
71	}
72	
73	// Resolve applies running > queued > remembered failure > observed > idle.
74	func Resolve(a Activity) State {
75		switch {
76		case a.Running:
77			return Running
78		case a.Queued:
79			return Queued
80		case a.Failed:
81			return Failed
82		}
83		return a.Observed
84	}

19	// extension rows of the view. Glyphs come from Glyph, never from literals.

1	package app
2	
3	import (
4		"time"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
12	)
13	
14	// blinkHalfPeriod is the blink's half period (D7: 1 Hz). A const: the phase formula
15	// must not change when a test shortens the chain's interval.
16	const blinkHalfPeriod = 500 * time.Millisecond
17	
18	// Intervals are vars so testutil.FastTimers can shorten them.
19	var (
20		animationFastInterval  = spinner.Dot.FPS
21		animationBlinkInterval = blinkHalfPeriod
22	)
23	
24	// blinkPhase reads the phase off the tick's own time, so every view blinks in step
25	// whatever the interval the chain currently runs at.
26	func blinkPhase(t time.Time) bool {
27		return (t.UnixMilli()/blinkHalfPeriod.Milliseconds())%2 == 0
28	}
29	
30	// cadence returns the interval the animation chain should run at, and false when
31	// nothing needs it. A running spinner needs the fast interval; a blink alone needs
32	// the slow one, unless static motion is requested (then the glyph stays steady).
33	func cadence(running, wantsBlink, static bool) (time.Duration, bool) {
34		switch {
35		case running:
36			return animationFastInterval, true
37		case wantsBlink && !static:
38			return animationBlinkInterval, true
39		default:
40			return 0, false
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// animationState is the one chain that moves anything on a row (D5, renamed D2).
45	type animationState struct {
46		seq      int           // identifies the live chain; a tick from another is dropped
47		ticking  bool          // a chain is alive
48		interval time.Duration // cadence of the live chain
49		frameIdx int
50		blinkOn  bool // true whenever no chain runs
51	}
52	
53	// animationTickMsg advances the animation. at is the tick's own time, from which
54	// the blink phase is read.
55	type animationTickMsg struct {
56		seq int
57		at  time.Time
58	}
59	
60	// animationEvery is tea.Every, a var so tests record the interval and inject the time.
61	var animationEvery = tea.Every
62	
63	// animationTick asks for the next tick of chain seq. It is on the clock's
64	// boundaries (tea.Every) so the blink phase alternates strictly. seq and d are
65	// captured by value: the Cmd never touches the router (Rule 110).
66	func animationTick(seq int, d time.Duration) tea.Cmd {
67		return animationEvery(d, func(t time.Time) tea.Msg {
68			return animationTickMsg{seq: seq, at: t}
69		})
70	}
71	
72	// animationFrame returns the current bare spinner frame.
73	func (a *App) animationFrame() string {
74		frames := spinner.Dot.Frames
75		return frames[a.anim.frameIdx%len(frames)]
76	}
77	
78	// frameMsg builds the animation message. It fills both readings of the frame —
79	// bare for a table cell (Rule 122), styled for a footer (Rule 128) — so the
80	// two cannot drift and internal/jobs needs to know nothing about styling.
81	func (a *App) frameMsg() jobs.FrameMsg {
82		frame := a.animationFrame()
83		return jobs.FrameMsg{
84			Frame:         frame,
85			RenderedFrame: theme.SpinnerStyle().Render(frame),
86			Blink:         a.anim.blinkOn,
87		}
88	}
89	
90	// sendFrameTo hands the current frame to one view: the view on screen on every
91	// tick, and a view entering the screen. No resize check: a frame never changes
92	// a footer's height.
93	func (a *App) sendFrameTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd {
94		view, ok := a.views[target]
95		if !ok {
96			return nil
97		}
98		updated, cmd := view.Update(a.frameMsg())
99		a.views[target] = updated
100		return cmd
101	}
102	
103	// ensureTick starts the chain when something needs one and none is alive, and
104	// replaces a slower chain by a faster one (a new seq makes the old tick stale).
105	// It returns nil otherwise, which makes it idempotent within one Update. It is
106	// the one place a chain is ever started (D5).
107	func (a *App) ensureTick() tea.Cmd {
108		d, ok := cadence(a.jobs.Running() > 0, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)
109		if !ok || (a.anim.ticking && a.anim.interval <= d) {
110			return nil
111		}
112		a.anim.ticking = true
113		a.anim.seq++
114		a.anim.interval = d
115		return animationTick(a.anim.seq, d)
116	}
117	
118	// handleAnimationTick advances the animation, reads the blink phase off the
119	// tick's own time, hands it to the view on screen, and renews the chain for as
120	// long as something needs it, at the cadence the need has now (a downgrade from
121	// fast to slow happens here, without a new seq).
122	//
123	// The chain stops by not being renewed. It never stops on an "off" phase: a row
124	// is left on a steady "on" glyph. The frame only moves while work runs.
125	func (a *App) handleAnimationTick(msg animationTickMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
126		if msg.seq != a.anim.seq {
127			return a, nil
128		}
129		running := a.jobs.Running() > 0
130		d, ok := cadence(running, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)
131		if !ok {
132			a.anim.ticking = false
133			if a.anim.blinkOn {
134				return a, nil
135			}
136			a.anim.blinkOn = true
137			return a, a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView)
138		}
139		if running {
140			a.anim.frameIdx = (a.anim.frameIdx + 1) % len(spinner.Dot.Frames)
141		}
142		a.anim.blinkOn = a.motionStatic || blinkPhase(msg.at)
143		a.anim.interval = d
144		return a, tea.Batch(a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView), animationTick(a.anim.seq, d))
145	}

181	// ChangedMsg carries what the registry holds to every view that might show it.
182	// It is the whole of the broadcast (D1): a view keeps its own copy of a
183	// snapshot rather than reading a pointer the router writes, so nothing is read
184	// from View() while something else is writing it.
185	//
186	// It is sent when the registry changes: a run started, a transition, a seal.
187	// The animation (the spinner frame, the blink phase) is not part of it: it
188	// travels in FrameMsg, to the view on screen only, so a tick never makes every
189	// held view rebuild its rows (DEVDESK-139).
190	//
191	// It lives in this package rather than in the router's so that every view can
192	// name it without importing the router, which imports them.
193	type ChangedMsg struct {
194		// Runs is a copy, oldest first, every context included. Filtering on the
195		// current one is the view's business (D8, FilterContext).
196		Runs []Run
197	
198		// Failures is a copy of what the registry remembers about failed targets,
199		// oldest first, every context included. Like Runs, it is read by the view
200		// and never written back.
201		Failures []Failure
202	}
203	
204	// Running counts the runs in the snapshot that have not settled. It saves every
205	// receiver the same three lines.
206	func (m ChangedMsg) Running() int {
207		return len(Unfinished(m.Runs))
208	}
209	
210	// FrameMsg says the animation moved: the spinner frame, the blink phase, or
211	// both. It carries no snapshot — ChangedMsg is for changes of the registry.
212	// The router sends it to the view on screen only (DEVDESK-139).
213	type FrameMsg struct {
214		Frame         string // bare, Rule 122 (a cell measures it)
215		RenderedFrame string // styled, Rule 128 (a footer takes it)
216		Blink         bool   // true = the "on" half of the blink
217	}

181	// ChangedMsg carries what the registry holds to every view that might show it.

183	// snapshot rather than reading a pointer the router writes, so nothing is read

13	// JobsStatusLine is what a footer says while work runs (D9).
14	//
15	// It is derived every frame rather than posted as a message, and Rule 128 says
16	// why: a batch outlives the three seconds a footer message gets, so a line set
17	// on the first repository would vanish while the tenth was still going.
18	//
19	// Three forms, and the third is a deliberate surrender:
20	//
21	//	Scanning — 3/12                     one kind, started by origin
22	//	Scanning — 3/12 · Syncing — 1/4      two kinds, both started by origin
23	//	3 jobs running — :jobs for details   anything else
24	//
25	// The degraded form is what a footer can honestly say about work it does not
26	// own. One line cannot carry four batches launched from three views, and a line
27	// that showed only the part it recognised would be worse than one that admits
28	// there is more.
29	//
30	// origin is the view asking. A view with no work of its own to name — the
31	// dashboard, which launches none — passes an empty ViewType and always gets the
32	// third form, which is the whole of what it has to say.
33	//
34	// It lives here rather than in internal/jobs because the third form names a
35	// command (`:jobs`), and that is interface copy; and here rather than in one
36	// view because two of them now say it.
37	func JobsStatusLine(runs []jobs.Run, origin command.ViewType) string {
38		live := jobs.Unfinished(runs)
39		if len(live) == 0 {
40			return ""
41		}
42	
43		mine := make([]jobs.Run, 0, len(live))
44		for _, run := range live {
45			if origin != "" && run.Origin == origin {
46				mine = append(mine, run)
47			}
48		}
49	
50		// Anything started elsewhere, or more than one batch of a kind, and the
51		// detailed line stops being able to tell the truth.
52		if len(mine) != len(live) || !oneRunPerKind(mine) {
53			return Plural(len(live), "job", "jobs") + " running — :jobs for details"
54		}
55	
56		parts := make([]string, 0, len(mine))
57		for _, kind := range jobs.Kinds() {
58			for _, run := range mine {
59				if run.Kind == kind {
60					parts = append(parts, run.Kind.Verb()+" — "+
61						strconv.Itoa(run.Done())+"/"+strconv.Itoa(run.Total()))
62				}
63			}
64		}
65		return strings.Join(parts, " · ")
66	}

68	// oneRunPerKind reports whether no two runs share a kind. Two scans at once are
69	// two counters, and "Scanning — 3/12 · Scanning — 1/2" reads as a bug.
70	func oneRunPerKind(runs []jobs.Run) bool {
71		seen := make(map[jobs.Kind]bool, len(runs))
72		for _, run := range runs {
73			if seen[run.Kind] {
74				return false
75			}
76			seen[run.Kind] = true
77		}
78		return true
79	}

81	// Plural writes a count with the right noun. Exported because three packages
82	// spell the same sentence now.
83	func Plural(n int, one, many string) string {
84		if n == 1 {

86		}
87		return strconv.Itoa(n) + " " + many
88	}

91	const rowSeparator = " · "

93	// Thresholds under which a part of the row line is dropped rather than cut to
94	// a stub nobody can read.
95	const (
96		minPathCols   = 6 // a ShortPath below this is just an ellipsis
97		minDetailCols = 8 // a detail below this says nothing; the progress stands alone
98	)

100	// RowDetail is what the footer says about the selected row: an activity glyph,
101	// a lead-in, the target (a path or an image reference) and a tail. Only the
102	// target is ever shortened as a path, which is why it is a field of its own.
103	type RowDetail struct{ Glyph, Lead, Target, Tail string }
104	
105	// IsZero reports whether the detail says nothing.
106	func (d RowDetail) IsZero() bool { return d == RowDetail{} }
107	
108	// head is everything before the target.
109	func (d RowDetail) head() string {
110		if d.Glyph == "" {
111			return d.Lead
112		}
113		return d.Glyph + " " + d.Lead
114	}
115	
116	// String is the detail at full length, the home directory folded.
117	func (d RowDetail) String() string { return d.head() + theme.FoldHome(d.Target) + d.Tail }
118	
119	// fit renders the detail in at most room columns. A path target shrinks first
120	// (never below minPathCols, even when the tail is long), then the end of the
121	// detail is cut. An image reference is not a path and is only ever cut.
122	func (d RowDetail) fit(room int) string {
123		full := d.String()
124		if theme.StringWidth(full) <= room {
125			return full
126		}
127		pathRoom := room - theme.StringWidth(d.head()) - theme.StringWidth(d.Tail)

129		// room first would only trade a readable prefix for an ellipsis.
130		if isPathTarget(d.Target) && (pathRoom >= minPathCols || d.Tail != "") {
131			full = d.head() + theme.ShortPath(d.Target, max(pathRoom, minPathCols)) + d.Tail
132		}
133		return theme.TruncateWidth(full, room)
134	}
135	
136	// isPathTarget tells a filesystem path from an image reference such as
137	// "registry/ns/app:1.2", which ShortPath would mangle.
138	func isPathTarget(target string) bool {
139		return filepath.IsAbs(target) || strings.HasPrefix(target, "~")
140	}
141	
142	// RowStatusLine composes the footer line for a selected row: its detail, then
143	// the batch progress, on one line of at most width columns. The progress is
144	// what gives way last; the detail is dropped whole when fewer than
145	// minDetailCols are left for it (or fewer than it needs, if it is shorter).
146	func RowStatusLine(detail RowDetail, progress string, width int) string {
147		switch {
148		case width <= 0:
149			return ""
150		case detail.IsZero():
151			return theme.TruncateWidth(progress, width)
152		case progress == "":
153			return detail.fit(width)
154		}
155		room := width - theme.StringWidth(rowSeparator) - theme.StringWidth(progress)
156		if room < min(minDetailCols, theme.StringWidth(detail.String())) {
157			return theme.TruncateWidth(progress, width)
158		}
159		return detail.fit(room) + rowSeparator + progress
160	}

76:Priorité sur une ligne, déjà décidée : **en cours > en file > échec > état observé > repos** (une seule fonction, `indicator.Resolve`). Quand un échec est masqué par une opération en cours, le footer l'ajoute en suffixe : `● Scanning ~/w/app/api · earlier failure: sync (see :jobs)`.
107:| a | **Sans couleur** (`NO_COLOR`, monochrome) : dix glyphes tous distincts | passe, avec une paire faible | `●` contre `◉` : un point plein contre un anneau à point, proches à petite taille dans certaines polices. | Action instantanée sur conteneur (stop, kill, remove) | `●` / `○` | Running | oui | `● Stopping web-1` |

Hypothèse : les libellés exacts (« last transcript line 4 s ago ») dépendent des données disponibles dans chaque vue ; seule la structure `glyphe + phrase` est prescrite.

Priorité sur une ligne, déjà décidée : **en cours > en file > échec > état observé > repos** (une seule fonction, `indicator.Resolve`). Quand un échec est masqué par une opération en cours, le footer l'ajoute en suffixe : `● Scanning ~/w/app/api · earlier failure: sync (see :jobs)`.

### 1.3 Choix tranchés (décision 7, 2026-11-06)

Les options étudiées avant la décision sont abandonnées ; il ne reste que le choix et sa raison.

- **Phase éteinte du clignotement : `○`, même couleur lavande.** Une capture figée se lit « quelque chose est là, en mouvement », jamais « rien » ; la couleur ne change pas (pas de scintillement de teinte) ; le contraste reste celui de l'état allumé (environ 7:1 sur la sélection). Écartés : `●` atténué en `ColorDim` (proche d'une cellule vide, échoue 3:1 : environ 2,5:1 sur le fond, 1,9:1 sous le curseur), `●` en `ColorText` (confondable avec un état terminé).
- **Conteneur `restarting` : `◕` orange fixe.** C'est un état observé, pas une opération lancée par DevDesk ; pas de dépendance au signal `WantsBlink` pour ce cas ; un `restarting` en boucle de crash change plus vite que le sondage docker, donc un clignotement synchronisé sur le tick serait trompeur ; `○` reste réservé à « en cours ».
- **« En file » : `◴` statique, `ColorActivityNeutral`.** Une file n'est pas une activité ; faire clignoter ce qui attend fait croire que ça avance, et un lot de 12 scans compterait 11 clignotants de plus sans information.
- **Conteneur `running` : aucune pastille** (D8). L'état nominal ne se colore pas (Rule 122, « color discipline ») ; la ligne garde son icône habituelle, et la pastille ne signale que ce qui s'écarte du nominal.

## 2. Test de lisibilité

Hypothèse : les rapports de contraste ci-dessous sont des calculs à la main (luminance relative WCAG) sur les valeurs par défaut Catppuccin (fond `#1e1e2e`, sélection `#313244`) ; `theme/contrast_test.go` doit les confirmer (A-01, critère 6).

### 2.1 Contraste des couleurs de pastille (critère WCAG 1.4.11, seuil 3:1)

| Couleur | Sur fond `#1e1e2e` | Sur sélection `#313244` |
|---|---|---|
| Running `#b4befe` | environ 9:1 | environ 7:1 |
| Neutral `#cdd6f4` | environ 11:1 | environ 8:1 |
| Suspended `#fab387` | environ 9:1 | environ 7:1 |
| Failed `#f38ba8` | environ 7:1 | environ 5:1 |
| (écarté) Dim `#585b70` | environ 2,5:1 : échoue | environ 1,9:1 : échoue |

Écart **corrigé** dans `stories.md` (A-13, critère 2 ; D7) : la version précédente prévoyait `unknown` en `DimStyle`. Cela échoue, et la sélection normale (§3.72) conserve la couleur de la cellule : un `◌` dim devient presque invisible sous le curseur. Correctif retenu et tranché : `unknown` et `created` en `ColorActivityNeutral` ; c'est le glyphe `◌` (anneau en pointillé) qui dit « vide ». Le test de contraste de A-01 vérifie chaque alias sur les deux fonds.

### 2.2 Les quatre épreuves

| # | Épreuve | Résultat | Où ça échoue, et le correctif |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | **Sans couleur** (`NO_COLOR`, monochrome) : dix glyphes tous distincts | passe, avec une paire faible | `●` contre `◉` : un point plein contre un anneau à point, proches à petite taille dans certaines polices. Ils se croisent dans `:jobs` et `:agent-usage` (en cours contre terminé), pas dans containers (un conteneur `running` n'a pas de pastille, D8). Correctifs : (1) le clignotement les sépare dès qu'on regarde deux secondes ; (2) le footer écrit l'état. L'utilisateur les distingue dans son terminal : **pas de repli `✓`** (D7). |
| b | **Sans mouvement** (capture figée, ou réglage `static`) | passe | La phase éteinte `○` est un anneau lavande, réservé : un cliché pris à l'instant « éteint » se lit « en cours ». En mode `static`, `●` fixe : le seul état qui bouge perd son mouvement mais garde glyphe et couleur, tous deux uniques parmi les états de la même vue. |
| c | **Daltonisme rouge/vert** (deutéranopie, protanopie) | passe | Le thème n'emploie aucun vert. Rouge `#f38ba8` et orange `#fab387` convergent vers des jaunes-gris proches : ils se distinguent par le glyphe (`⊗` contre `◐`/`◕`), c'est la raison d'être de la règle. Lavande et texte convergent aussi vers des gris-bleu : `●`/`○` contre `◉` les sépare. |
| d | **Sous le curseur, sélection normale** | passe | La Rule 118 révisée (§3.72) garde la couleur de chaque cellule, repeinte sur `ColorTableLineSelected` ; le gras est ajouté. Toutes les couleurs de pastille dépassent 3:1 dessus (§2.1). Le clignotement continue : la phase est lue au rendu. |
| d' | **Sous une ligne colorée en entier** (erreur de containers, `busy`, sévérité) | passe, par le glyphe | La couleur de la pastille tombe (fond plein `ColorError`, texte `ColorBlack`). Le glyphe reste : `⊗` noir sur rouge, et pour l'action en cours `●`/`○` qui alterne dans le texte de la cellule (raisonnement de `rowLine` pour `busy`, Q6 de l'architect). |

### 2.3 Cas où l'état est ambigu au seul coup d'œil, et réponse

- Repos (icône de ligne) contre `◌` (vide, créé, inconnu) : l'icône de repos est un glyphe Nerd Font de type de ligne, `◌` est un anneau en pointillé : distincts. Si la vue n'a pas d'icône, le repos est une cellule vide (jamais `◌`).
- `⊗` rouge pour `exited` non nul et pour `dead` : même glyphe, sens « cassé ». Le statut texte du conteneur (colonne Status) et le footer distinguent les deux.

### 2.4 Matrice de coexistence (ce qui doit rester distinguable dans une même vue)

| Vue | États qui coexistent |
|---|---|
| `:jobs` | `●`/`○`, `◴`, `⊗`, `◉`, `⊘`, `⊖` |
| `ws`, `:sec`, OCI | `●`/`○`, `◴`, `⊗`, icône de repos |
| `:agent-usage` | `●`/`○`, `◐`, `◉`, `◌` |
| containers | icône de repos (conteneur `running`), `◕`, `◐`, `◌`, `⊗`, `⊖`, `●`/`○` (action instantanée) |

Chaque ligne a des glyphes deux à deux distincts ; la seule paire faible est `●` contre `◉` (a), qui ne se croise plus dans containers.

## 3. Maquettes

Conventions : seule la première colonne est spécifiée ; les autres colonnes sont illustratives. Largeurs indicatives (cadre de 60 et de 120 colonnes), à confirmer par `RenderedWidth()` (Rule 116) à l'implémentation. `←` à droite d'un cadre est une annotation, hors écran. La phase affichée est l'allumée ; une ligne est redessinée en phase éteinte quand c'est utile. La ligne sélectionnée est repeinte entièrement sur `ColorTableLineSelected`, gras.

555	The footer can say what the selected row is doing, in the same words the
556	activity column's state implies. **No view is wired to it yet.** The pieces
557	below exist and are tested; the views adopt them in the migration stories
558	(A-06 onward).
559	
560	**`jobs.ActiveOn(runs, context, target, kinds...) []jobs.Active`**
561	(`internal/jobs/active.go`). The running and queued items on a target in a
562	context: running first, then queued, each group in run order. Target is
563	normalised with `TargetKey` on both sides. No `kinds` keeps every kind. Items
564	are copied without their cancel hook. No match returns nil.
565	
566	**`Status.Detail` and `RowDetail`.** `Status` gains a `Detail RowDetail`
567	(`footer_message.go`); `Status.Text` then becomes the batch progress that
568	follows it. `RowDetail{Glyph, Lead, Target, Tail}` is one sentence; `Target` is
569	a field of its own because only a path is ever shortened.
570	
571	- **`RowStatusLine(detail, progress, width)`** (`jobs_status.go`) joins

The footer can say what the selected row is doing, in the same words the
activity column's state implies. **No view is wired to it yet.** The pieces
below exist and are tested; the views adopt them in the migration stories
(A-06 onward).

**`jobs.ActiveOn(runs, context, target, kinds...) []jobs.Active`**
(`internal/jobs/active.go`). The running and queued items on a target in a
context: running first, then queued, each group in run order. Target is
normalised with `TargetKey` on both sides. No `kinds` keeps every kind. Items
are copied without their cancel hook. No match returns nil.

**`Status.Detail` and `RowDetail`.** `Status` gains a `Detail RowDetail`
(`footer_message.go`); `Status.Text` then becomes the batch progress that
follows it. `RowDetail{Glyph, Lead, Target, Tail}` is one sentence; `Target` is
a field of its own because only a path is ever shortened.

- **`RowStatusLine(detail, progress, width)`** (`jobs_status.go`) joins
  them as `<detail> · <progress>` (`rowSeparator`) on at most `width` columns.
  Zero detail: the progress alone. No progress: the detail alone.
- **Cut order.** A path target shrinks first with `theme.ShortPath`, never
  below `minPathCols` (6), then the end of the detail is truncated. An image
  reference is not a path (`isPathTarget`: absolute or `~`) and is only
  truncated. If fewer than `minDetailCols` (8) columns are left for the detail
  (or fewer than it needs, when it is shorter), the detail is dropped whole and
  the progress stands alone.
- **Precedence is unchanged:** error → warning → info → status. `Detail` is
  part of the status, so a footer message still wins over it.
- **A detail with a glyph suppresses the spinner:** the row's own dot already
  moves.
- **East Asian width.** `centerLine` pads by `lipgloss.Width`, which counts
  ambiguous glyphs as one cell. `View` shrinks its target width by

  columns for `runewidth` too.

**One constructor of sentences** (`row_activity.go`). The view fills a
`RowQuery{Runs, Failures, Context, Target, Kinds, Observed, ObservedText}`

- **`RowState(q)`**: the `indicator.State` for the activity column, no text.

  `resolveRow`, so the glyph in the table and the sentence in the footer cannot

860	`jobsChanged` is what a launch site or a transition calls after writing to the
861	registry: `ChangedMsg` to every held view, `FrameMsg` to the view on screen. The
862	`Update` wrapper then makes sure a chain is alive; the three are separate, and
863	none implies another.
864	
865	This is what removes the four hand-stamped frames, and with them the failure
866	each of them could produce: a chain that died on the first idle tick with
867	nothing able to restart it, leaving the spinner frozen on the frame it died at.
868	
869	#### Row chains still outside the router
870	
871	Four row-animation chains still live in views. They are **declared exceptions**
872	in `TestRowAnimationChainsOutsideTheRouterAreDeclared`; the list may only shrink,
873	and a stale entry fails the test:
874	
875	| Chain | Removed by |
876	|---|---|
877	| `oci_resources` `AdvanceSpinner` on the four OCI tables | A-09b |
878	| `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (OCI registry browser) | A-09a |
879	| `netdiag` `portsSpinnerCmd` | A-12 |
880	| `containers` `AdvanceSpinner` | A-14 |
881	
882	A-16 then closes the exceptions. `TestOnlyTheRouterBuildsAFrameMsg` and
883	`TestTheAnimationChainUnderARealProgram` (a real `tea.Program`, meant for
884	`-race`) complete the guard rails.
885	
886	#### What the redraw costs
887	
888	`DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1 go test ./internal/app -run TestMeasureRedrawCost -v`
889	counts the bytes Bubble Tea's renderer writes to an `io.Writer` on a simulated
890	120x40 terminal — not a real terminal. Opt-in; the test is skipped otherwise.
891	
892	| Animation | Bytes emitted |
893	|---|---|
894	| no animated row | 0 B/s |
895	| 1 row blinking at 1 Hz | 376 B/s |
896	| 20 rows blinking at 1 Hz | 5 809 B/s |
897	| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 1 row | 1 880 B/s |
898	| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 20 rows | 29 049 B/s |
899	
900	Nothing animated costs nothing, and a 1 Hz blink costs about a fifth of the
901	10 Hz spinner it sits beside.
902	
903	
904	### The `:jobs` view — `internal/ui/jobsview`
905	
906	The reader's side of the registry, and it owns nothing: it starts no work, holds
907	no timer and fetches nothing. Its rows are the snapshot, so there is nothing to
908	refresh — `ctrl+r` is absent rather than greyed, because there is no operation
909	behind it to be unavailable.
910	
911	Two levels (D2): the runs, and `→` on one of them for its targets. A level
912	rather than a pair of tabs — the second table is *about* a row of the first, so
913	it is reached the way every drill-down in the application is (Rule 111), and the
914	trail is a breadcrumb below the table (Rule 123).
915	
916	| | Columns |
917	|---|---|
918	| runs | state glyph (untitled, `IconColumnWidth`), Kind, Label, Progress, State, Started |
919	| targets | state glyph, Target, State, Detail |
920	
921	**The first column is the state, not the kind**, and it is also where the
922	spinner goes — the containers table's shape. A jobs list is scanned to find the
923	run that failed and the one still going, so the glyph answers the question the
924	reader arrived with; the Kind column says in a word what sort of work it was,
925	and carries the state in its `Search` so `/failed` and `/scan` both work while
926	the glyph column stays out of the filter (Rule 125).
927	
928	A state glyph colours by the semantic status styles rather than by a
929	`theme.IconStyle` role. Roles exist for icons naming an *object* — a namespace, a
930	repository, an image — where the palette should be able to tell them apart; a
931	state already has a colour, and five new roles would give a theme five ways to
932	make `failed` not red.
933	
934	**The frame rides on the row.** `runRow`/`itemRow` wrap the model value with the
935	frame, because the columns are built once and close over nothing — the same
936	reason `oci_resources` has `imageRow`. It is the router's frame, taken bare from
937	`jobs.FrameMsg` (the view is on screen whenever it receives one; `ChangedMsg`
938	carries only the runs): using `datatable`'s own `AdvanceSpinner` here would be a
939	second chain beside the one D5 exists to keep single.
940	
941	**The context is passed, not read.** `jobsview.New(cfg, contextName)` takes the
942	name from the router, for D68's reason one screen over: the router is what knows
943	which context is current. The view filters the snapshot on it (`FilterContext`),
944	so a switch hides runs rather than dropping them — and the router rebuilds every
945	view on a switch anyway, so the cached name cannot go stale.
946	
947	`K` is state-aware at both levels (Rule 130) and greyed with a **named** reason:
948	"This run has already finished", "A delete cannot be stopped once it has
949	started". The refusal is never silent — pressing a greyed key says why in the

`DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1 go test ./internal/app -run TestMeasureRedrawCost -v`
counts the bytes Bubble Tea's renderer writes to an `io.Writer` on a simulated
120x40 terminal — not a real terminal. Opt-in; the test is skipped otherwise.

| Animation | Bytes emitted |
|---|---|
| no animated row | 0 B/s |
| 1 row blinking at 1 Hz | 376 B/s |
| 20 rows blinking at 1 Hz | 5 809 B/s |
| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 1 row | 1 880 B/s |
| reference: spinner at 10 Hz, 20 rows | 29 049 B/s |

Nothing animated costs nothing, and a 1 Hz blink costs about a fifth of the
10 Hz spinner it sits beside.

The reader's side of the registry, and it owns nothing: it starts no work, holds
no timer and fetches nothing. Its rows are the snapshot, so there is nothing to
refresh — `ctrl+r` is absent rather than greyed, because there is no operation
behind it to be unavailable.

Two levels (D2): the runs, and `→` on one of them for its targets. A level
rather than a pair of tabs — the second table is *about* a row of the first, so
it is reached the way every drill-down in the application is (Rule 111), and the
trail is a breadcrumb below the table (Rule 123).

| | Columns |
|---|---|
| runs | state glyph (untitled, `IconColumnWidth`), Kind, Label, Progress, State, Started |
| targets | state glyph, Target, State, Detail |

run that failed and the one still going, so the glyph answers the question the

which context is current. The view filters the snapshot on it (`FilterContext`),
so a switch hides runs rather than dropping them — and the router rebuilds every
view on a switch anyway, so the cached name cannot go stale.
